newsitem.title: USA: Investors scoop up US corp debt issues,more coming.
newsitem.headline: Investors scoop up US corp debt issues,more coming.

text.p: More corporate bond issues are seen on the horizon as paper hungry investors quickly absorb new supply but still clamor for more, dealers said.
"There's a very constructive tone in the market and deals have been met with good demand," one syndicate source said.

On Wednesday, Petronas launched a three-part $1.5 billion global deal via CS First Boston and Salomon Brothers. The size of the deal was boosted from an initial $1.0 billion to meet growing investor demand, sources said.
The first tranche consist of $600 million in five-year debt with price talk seen in the 38 to 40 basis points arena.
The second tranche is for $600 million in 10-year bonds with price talk in the 57 to 59 basis points area.
The third tranche consist of $300 million in 30-year bonds which are expected to yield a spread of 85 basis points.
Panenergy is also expected to tap the market with $100 million in 10-year debt via Chase Securities. Price talk is seen at 60 basis points over Treasuries, dealers said.
Allegiance Healthcare is expected to price $500 million in a three-part debt offering via Goldman Sachs, sources said.
Also, Kohl Department Stores and Goodyear Tires are each expected to issue $100 million in debt, syndicate sources said.
Meanwhile, dealers said the market is going to be hit with an avalanche of asset-backed issuance adding even more supply to the market.
"There's a lot of paper out there. ... There's about $7.0 billion in asset-backed issues coming to market," one dealer said.

Lower financing rates and a rapidly approaching end to the calendar year should push issuance to the forefront now as upcoming holidays, coupled with thinly staffed desks, make it virtually impossible to structure new deals, dealers said.
In high-yield issues, Goss Graphic Systems' $225 million in B2/B-rated senior subordianted notes due 2006 via CS First Boston.
Paging Network Inc is expected to price $350 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2008 via Goldman Sachs.
Among other foreign issues, Banco Santander is expected to price $150 million in 10-year subordinated yankee notes.
Banco Nationale de Paris is expected to tap the market with $350 million in 10-year subordinated yankee debt via Salomon Brothers, in early October.

On Tuesday, WMX Technologies priced $300 million in 10-year debt via Merrill Lynch & Co to yield 53 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. The deal was upped in size from an initial $200 million to meet investor demand.
Painewebber, Bear Stearns and Becton Dickinson were among other issuers who priced debt in Tuesday's business.
Dealers said Tuesday's deals were met with very good reception by investors.
In the government market, the U.S. Treasury 30-year bond is up 6/32 at 99-15/32 to yield 6.79 percent.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
